analysis.title: Weekly commentary: Inflation: beyond the Mideast energy shock
key_insights: BII thinks the energy shock's impact on U.S. inflation has peaked. Brent, gasoline and diesel prices fell sharply this month, which should ease headline and core inflation via lower transportation services prices.
BII estimates the shock added 1.5 percentage points to U.S. headline inflation at its September peak. The contribution should reverse to a 0.8 percentage point drag by year-end 2027.
Europe's inflation relief will lag the U.S. because earlier natural gas price increases are still feeding through to consumers. The U.S. is a net energy exporter with limited gas price exposure.
In the U.S., a tight labor market and wage growth of around 4% keep core services inflation elevated. BII expects core inflation closer to 3% than the Fed's 2% target.
Markets price a December Fed hike, in line with BII, plus as many as two more next year. BII thinks the latter is overdone and expects one more hike in H1 2027.
BII favors short- and medium-term U.S. Treasuries for income and protection against rate swings. It is overweight short-term Treasuries and neutral long-term Treasuries.
BII recently strengthened its strategic overweight on inflation-linked bonds to hedge supply-driven inflation risks, while remaining neutral tactically on global inflation-linked bonds.

AI sentiment stayed weak despite solid Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's record IPO. The Nasdaq fell 10% and the S&P 500 entered correction territory, with CEO succession and circular financing concerns cited.
U.S. 10-year yield fell to 4.94%, about 40bp below October's 24-year high. The 2-year yield fell to 4.64%.
Tactical positioning: neutral U.S., Europe, UK, Japan and China equities, overweight EM equities, underweight Japanese government bonds and long-term IG credit, overweight EM local debt.
BII expects the ECB to raise rates next month, with the outlook beyond December depending on energy pass-through to underlying inflation.
Week ahead: October PCE and second-estimate GDP on Nov. 25, plus consumer confidence and flash PMIs, are the key checks on services inflation and Fed tightening.
